title.raw: 《陳涉世家》 House of Chen She

sentences.zh: 陳勝者，陽城人也，字涉。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng was a man from Yangcheng. His courtesy name was She.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng was a native of Yangcheng, styled She.

sentences.zh: 吳廣者，陽夏人也，字叔。

translations.literal: Wu Guang was a man from Yangxia. His courtesy name was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang was a native of Yangxia, styled Shu.

sentences.zh: 陳涉少時，嘗與人傭耕，輟耕之壟上，悵恨久之，曰：「茍富貴，無相忘。」

translations.literal: Chen She young time, once with people hired plow, paused plow on ridge, melancholy resent long time, said: 'If rich noble, no mutually forget.'
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, Chen She once worked as a hired laborer plowing fields alongside others. He stopped his plowing and climbed to the top of a ridge, where he stood brooding for a long while before saying, 'If any of us should ever become wealthy and noble, let us not forget one another.'

sentences.zh: 庸者笑而應曰：「若為庸耕，何富貴也？」

translations.literal: Hired ones laugh respond said: 'You as hired plow, what rich noble?'
translations.idiomatic: The other laborers laughed and replied, 'You are nothing but a hired hand plowing fields — how could you ever become wealthy and noble?'

sentences.zh: 陳涉太息曰：「嗟乎，燕雀安知鴻鵠之志哉！」

translations.literal: Chen She sighed deeply and said: 'Alas! How can sparrows and swallows know the ambitions of swans and wild geese!'
translations.idiomatic: Chen She heaved a deep sigh and said, 'Alas! How can sparrows and swallows know the ambitions of swans and wild geese?'

sentences.zh: 二世元年七月，發閭左適戍漁陽，九百人屯大澤鄉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of the Second Emperor, they conscripted men from the neighborhoods to the left for garrison duty at Yuyang. Nine hundred men were stationed at Daze Township.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of the Second Emperor's reign, a levy was raised to conscript commoners for garrison duty at Yuyang. Nine hundred men were assembled at Daze Township.

sentences.zh: 陳勝、吳廣皆次當行，為屯長。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were both next in line to go, so they became the camp chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were both among those called up, and they were appointed as squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，道不通，度已失期。

translations.literal: They encountered great rains, the roads became impassable, and they estimated they had already missed their deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains fell without cease, the roads became impassable, and they reckoned they had already missed the deadline.

sentences.zh: 失期，法皆斬。

translations.literal: Missing the deadline meant execution by law for all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, the penalty for missing the deadline was death for all.

sentences.zh: 陳勝、吳廣乃謀曰：「今亡亦死，舉大計亦死，等死，死國可乎？」

translations.literal: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang then plotted together and said: 'If we flee now we still die; if we rise in revolt we also die. Since it is the same death, may we not die for the state?'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang conferred in secret: 'If we flee now, we die. If we rise up in revolt, we also die. Since death awaits us either way, would it not be better to die fighting for our country?'

sentences.zh: 陳勝曰：「天下苦秦久矣。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng said: 'World suffers Qin long already.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng said, 'The empire has suffered under Qin for far too long.

sentences.zh: 吾聞二世少子也，不當立，當立者乃公子扶蘇。

translations.literal: I have heard that the Second Emperor is the younger son and should not have been enthroned. The one who should have been enthroned is Prince Fusu.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Second Emperor is the younger son and was never meant to take the throne. The rightful heir was Prince Fusu.

sentences.zh: 扶蘇以數諫故，上使外將兵。

translations.literal: Because Fu Su repeatedly remonstrated, the emperor sent him outside to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fusu remonstrated with his father on many occasions, the emperor sent him away to command troops on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今或聞無罪，二世殺之。

translations.literal: Now some have heard that though he was guiltless, the Second Emperor killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now word has it that, though Fusu committed no crime, the Second Emperor had him killed.

sentences.zh: 百姓多聞其賢，未知其死也。

translations.literal: The common people have heard much of his worthiness, but do not know he is dead.
translations.idiomatic: The common people have heard much of his virtue but have not yet learned of his death.

sentences.zh: 項燕為楚將，數有功，愛士卒，楚人憐之。

translations.literal: Xiang Yan was a Chu general who repeatedly achieved merit and loved his officers and soldiers. The Chu people pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yan served as a general of Chu, won many victories, and cared deeply for his soldiers. The people of Chu mourned him.

sentences.zh: 或以為死，或以為亡。

translations.literal: Some think he is dead, some think he has fled.
translations.idiomatic: Some believe he is dead; others say he has fled into exile.

sentences.zh: 今誠以吾眾詐自稱公子扶蘇、項燕，為天下唱，宜多應者。」

translations.literal: Now if we truly have our multitude falsely proclaim Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan and raise the call for the empire, many should respond.'
translations.idiomatic: If we now rally our men and raise a banner in the names of Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, issuing a call to the empire, many will surely answer.'

sentences.zh: 吳廣以為然。

translations.literal: Wu Guang thought this was right.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃行卜。

translations.literal: They then performed divination.
translations.idiomatic: They went to consult a diviner.

sentences.zh: 卜者知其指意，曰：「足下事皆成，有功。

translations.literal: Diviner knew their intent, said: 'Your excellency matters all succeed, have merit.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner perceived their true intent and said, 'All your endeavors will succeed, and you will win great merit.

sentences.zh: 然足下卜之鬼乎！」

translations.literal: But your excellency divined ghosts!'
translations.idiomatic: But have you consulted the spirits about this?'

sentences.zh: 陳勝、吳廣喜，念鬼，曰：「此教我先威眾耳。」

translations.literal: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were delighted. Thinking of ghosts, they said: 'This means we should first overawe the multitude.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were delighted. Reflecting on the mention of spirits, they said, 'He is telling us to first overawe the men with supernatural signs.'

sentences.zh: 乃丹書帛曰「陳勝王」，置人所罾魚腹中。

translations.literal: Then cinnabar wrote silk 'Chen Sheng king', placed in people caught fish belly.
translations.idiomatic: So they wrote 'Chen Sheng shall be king' in cinnabar on a strip of silk and slipped it into the belly of a fish that someone had caught in a net.

sentences.zh: 卒買魚烹食，得魚腹中書，固以怪之矣。

translations.literal: The soldiers bought the fish, cooked and ate it, and found the writing in the fish belly. They indeed marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When the soldiers bought the fish and cooked it, they discovered the writing inside its belly and were already astonished.

sentences.zh: 又彊令吳廣之次所旁叢祠中，夜篝火，狐鳴呼曰「大楚興，陳勝王」。

translations.literal: Again forced Wu Guang lodging place beside grove shrine, night bonfire, fox cry call 'Great Chu rise, Chen Sheng king'.
translations.idiomatic: Then they had Wu Guang steal into a shrine in a thicket near the camp at night. There he lit a fire inside a basket and, imitating the cry of a fox, called out, 'Great Chu shall rise again! Chen Sheng shall be king!'

sentences.zh: 卒皆夜驚恐。

translations.literal: All the soldiers were startled and terrified at night.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were all terrified in the night.

sentences.zh: 旦日，卒中往往語，皆指目陳勝。

translations.literal: The next morning, the soldiers often talked among themselves, all pointing their eyes toward Chen Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning, the soldiers whispered among themselves, casting sidelong glances at Chen Sheng and pointing him out to one another.

sentences.zh: 吳廣素愛人，士卒多為用者。

translations.literal: Wu Guang usually loved people, and many officers and soldiers were willing to be used by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang had always treated others with kindness, and many of the soldiers were devoted to him.

sentences.zh: 將尉醉，廣故數言欲亡，忿恚尉，令辱之，以激怒其眾。

translations.literal: The commandant was drunk. Guang intentionally repeatedly said he wanted to flee, enraging the commandant and causing him to insult Guang, in order to stir up anger among the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the commanding officer was drunk, Wu Guang deliberately spoke again and again of deserting, provoking the officer into a fury so that he would publicly humiliate him — all to stir the anger of the men.

sentences.zh: 尉果笞廣。

translations.literal: The commandant indeed flogged Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The officer did indeed have Wu Guang flogged.

sentences.zh: 尉劍挺，廣起，奪而殺尉。

translations.literal: The commandant drew his sword. Guang rose up, seized it, and killed the commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the officer drew his sword, Wu Guang sprang up, seized it, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 陳勝佐之，并殺兩尉。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng assisted him, and together they killed the two commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng rushed to his aid, and together they slew both officers.

sentences.zh: 召令徒屬曰：「公等遇雨，皆已失期，失期當斬。

translations.literal: Summoned ordered followers said: 'You gentlemen encountered rain, all already missed deadline, missed deadline should behead.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned all their men and addressed them: 'You have been delayed by the rains and have already missed the deadline. The penalty for missing the deadline is execution.

sentences.zh: 藉弟令毋斬，而戍死者固十六七。

translations.literal: Even if by special order you were spared beheading, still six or seven out of ten garrison soldiers die on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Even if by special order you were spared beheading, still six or seven out of every ten sent to garrison the frontier die there regardless.

sentences.zh: 且壯士不死即已，死即舉大名耳，王侯將相寧有種乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, a bold man either does not die at all, or if he dies he raises a great name; can kings, marquises, generals, and ministers have breeding?'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a bold man either does not die at all, or if he dies, he makes a great name. Are kings, marquises, generals, and ministers born to their stations?'

sentences.zh: 徒屬皆曰：「敬受命。」

translations.literal: Followers all said: 'Respectfully receive command.'
translations.idiomatic: The men all answered, 'We are at your command.'

sentences.zh: 乃詐稱公子扶蘇、項燕，從民欲也。

translations.literal: Then falsely claimed young lord Fu Su, Xiang Yan, followed people's desire.
translations.idiomatic: They then raised their banner in the names of Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, following the will of the people.

sentences.zh: 袒右，稱大楚。

translations.literal: They bared their right arms and called themselves Great Chu.
translations.idiomatic: They bared their right shoulders as a pledge and proclaimed themselves the army of Great Chu.

sentences.zh: 為壇而盟，祭以尉首。

translations.literal: They made an altar and formed an alliance, sacrificing with the commandant's head.
translations.idiomatic: They built an earthen altar and swore a solemn oath, offering the officers' heads as a sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 陳勝自立為將軍，吳廣為都尉。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng established himself as general, and Wu Guang as deputy commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng declared himself general, and Wu Guang was made commandant.

sentences.zh: 攻大澤鄉，收而攻蘄。

translations.literal: They attacked Daze Township, took it, and then attacked Qi.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Daze Township, took it, and then marched on Qi.

sentences.zh: 蘄下，乃令符離人葛嬰將兵徇蘄以東。

translations.literal: Qi fell. They then ordered Ge Ying of Fuli to lead troops and sweep eastward from Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, they ordered Ge Ying, a man of Fuli, to lead troops and sweep the territory east of Qi.

sentences.zh: 攻銍、酇、苦、柘、譙皆下之。

translations.literal: They attacked Zhi, Zan, Ku, Zhe, and Qiao, and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked and captured Zhi, Zan, Ku, Zhe, and Qiao, taking each one in turn.

sentences.zh: 行收兵。

translations.literal: Along the way they gathered troops.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way, they gathered more troops to their cause.

sentences.zh: 比至陳，車六七百乘，騎千餘，卒數萬人。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived at Chen, they had six or seven hundred chariots, over a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the city of Chen, their force had swelled to six or seven hundred chariots, over a thousand cavalry, and tens of thousands of infantry.

sentences.zh: 攻陳，陳守令皆不在，獨守丞與戰譙門中。

translations.literal: They attacked Chen. Chen's defending prefect was not present, and only the deputy prefect fought them in the Qiao gate.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Chen. The governor and the magistrate were both absent; only the deputy governor remained to fight them at the city gate.

sentences.zh: 弗勝，守丞死，乃入據陳。

translations.literal: They were not victorious. The deputy prefect died, and then they entered and occupied Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy could not hold them back and was killed, and the rebels entered and occupied Chen.

sentences.zh: 數日，號令召三老、豪傑與皆來會計事。

translations.literal: After several days, by proclamation they summoned the village elders and outstanding men to all come meet and discuss matters.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, they issued a proclamation summoning the local elders and men of influence to gather and deliberate on the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 三老、豪傑皆曰：「將軍身被堅執銳，伐無道，誅暴秦，復立楚國之社稷，功宜為王。」

translations.literal: Village elders, outstanding men all said: 'General body wears armor grasps sharp weapons, attacks unrighteous, executes violent Qin, reestablishes Chu state altars soil, merit should become king.'
translations.idiomatic: The elders and men of standing all declared, 'The general has donned armor and taken up arms to strike down tyranny, punish the brutal Qin, and restore the altars of the state of Chu. By such merit, he deserves to be made king.'

sentences.zh: 陳涉乃立為王，號為張楚。

translations.literal: Chen She then established himself as king, with the title 'Zhang Chu.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen She was thus enthroned as king, and his state was named Zhang Chu — 'Expanding Chu.'

sentences.zh: 當此時，諸郡縣苦秦吏者，皆刑其長吏，殺之以應陳涉。

translations.literal: At this time, the various commanderies and counties that suffered under Qin officials all punished their chief officials and killed them to respond to Chen She.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, across the commanderies and counties that had long suffered under Qin's officials, the people punished and killed their local administrators to answer Chen She's call.

sentences.zh: 乃以吳叔為假王，監諸將以西擊滎陽。

translations.literal: They then made Wu Shu acting king to oversee the various generals in attacking Xingyang to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang was appointed acting king to supervise the generals in the westward campaign against Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 令陳人武臣、張耳、陳餘徇趙地，令汝陰人鄧宗徇九江郡。

translations.literal: They ordered wuchen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu of Chen to sweep through Zhao lands, and ordered Deng Zong of Ruyin to sweep through Jiujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu — all men of Chen — were ordered to subdue the Zhao territories, while Deng Zong of Ruyin was sent to pacify the Commandery of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 當此時，楚兵數千人為聚者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: At this time, Chu troops formed gatherings of several thousand each, too numerous to count.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, bands of Chu soldiers numbering in the thousands sprang up everywhere, too many to count.

sentences.zh: 葛嬰至東城，立襄彊為楚王。

translations.literal: Ge Ying arrived at Dongcheng and established Xiang Qiang as Chu king.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ying reached Dongcheng and set up Xiang Qiang as the King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 嬰後聞陳王已立，因殺襄彊，還報。

translations.literal: Ying later heard that the Chen king was already established, so he killed Xiang Qiang and returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Ying later learned that Chen She had already been crowned king, he killed Xiang Qiang and returned to report.

sentences.zh: 至陳，陳王誅殺葛嬰。

translations.literal: When he arrived at Chen, the Chen king executed Ge Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Ying arrived in Chen, the king had him executed.

sentences.zh: 陳王令魏人周市北徇魏地。

translations.literal: The Chen king ordered Zhou Shi of Wei to sweep north through Wei lands.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen ordered Zhou Shi, a man of Wei, to march north and pacify the Wei territories.

sentences.zh: 吳廣圍滎陽。

translations.literal: Wu Guang besieged Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang laid siege to Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 李由為三川守，守滎陽，吳叔弗能下。

translations.literal: Li You was governor of Sanchuan and defended Xingyang. Wu Shu could not conquer it.
translations.idiomatic: Li You, the Governor of Sanchuan, defended Xingyang, and Wu Guang could not take it.

sentences.zh: 陳王徵國之豪傑與計，以上蔡人房君蔡賜為上柱國。

translations.literal: The Chen king summoned the state's outstanding men to consult on plans and made Cai Ci, Lord of Fang from Shangcai, Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen summoned the outstanding men of the realm to consult on strategy and appointed Cai Ci, Lord of Fang from Shangcai, as Supreme Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 周文，陳之賢人也，嘗為項燕軍視日，事春申君，自言習兵，陳王與之將軍印，西擊秦。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen was a worthy man of Chen. He had once observed the days for Xiang Yan's army and served Chunshen Jun. He claimed to be practiced in military matters, so the Chen king gave him a general's seal to attack Qin to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen was a man of ability from Chen who had once served as a diviner for Xiang Yan's army and had been in the retinue of Lord Chunshen. He claimed expertise in military affairs, so the King of Chen bestowed upon him a general's seal and sent him west to attack Qin.

sentences.zh: 行收兵至關，車千乘，卒數十萬，至戲，軍焉。

translations.literal: Along the way he gathered troops until he reached the pass, with a thousand chariots and tens of thousands of foot soldiers. He arrived at Xi and camped there.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering troops along the march, by the time he reached the passes his army numbered a thousand chariots and several tens of thousands of soldiers. He advanced to Xi and encamped.

sentences.zh: 秦令少府章邯免酈山徒、人奴產子生，悉發以擊楚大軍，盡敗之。

translations.literal: Qin ordered Zhang Han of the Lesser Treasury to release the convicts from Mount Li and their born children, and send them all to attack the Chu great army. They completely defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ordered the Privy Treasurer Zhang Han to pardon the convict laborers at Mount Li and the sons born to slaves, arming them all and sending them against the great army of Chu. They routed it utterly.

sentences.zh: 周文敗，走出關，止次曹陽二三月。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen was defeated and fled out of the pass. He stopped and camped at Caoyang for two or three months.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen was defeated and fled east out of the passes, halting at Caoyang where he held his position for two or three months.

sentences.zh: 章邯追敗之，復走次澠池十餘日。

translations.literal: Zhang Han pursued and defeated him. He fled again and camped at Mianchi for over ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han pursued and defeated him again. Zhou Wen retreated to Mianchi, where he held out for just over ten days.

sentences.zh: 章邯擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Han attacked and greatly broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han struck once more and crushed his forces.

sentences.zh: 周文自剄，軍遂不戰。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen cut his own throat, and the army then ceased fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen cut his own throat, and his army disbanded without further resistance.

sentences.zh: 武臣到邯鄲，自立為趙王，陳餘為大將軍，張耳、召騷為左右丞相。

translations.literal: wuchen arrived at Handan and established himself as Zhao king. Chen Yu became great general, and Zhang Er and Zhao Sao became left and right chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen arrived at Handan and declared himself King of Zhao. Chen Yu was made Grand General, and Zhang Er and Zhao Sao became the Left and Right Chancellors.

sentences.zh: 陳王怒，捕系武臣等家室，欲誅之。

translations.literal: The Chen king was angry. He captured and bound wuchen and others' families, intending to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen was furious. He seized the families of Wu Chen and his associates, intending to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 柱國曰：「秦未亡而誅趙王將相家屬，此生一秦也。

translations.literal: Pillar state said: 'Qin not yet perished but execute Zhao king generals chancellors families, this creates one Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Pillar of State objected: 'If, while Qin has not yet fallen, you execute the families of the King of Zhao and his generals and ministers, you will only create another Qin.

sentences.zh: 不如因而立之。」

translations.literal: Not as good take advantage establish them.'
translations.idiomatic: Better to accept the situation and recognize him.'

sentences.zh: 陳王乃遣使者賀趙，而徙系武臣等家屬宮中，而封耳子張敖為成都君，趣趙兵亟入關。

translations.literal: The Chen king then sent envoys to congratulate Zhao. He moved wuchen and others' bound families into the palace, and sealed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu. He urged the Zhao troops to quickly enter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen then sent envoys to congratulate Zhao. He moved the detained families of Wu Chen and the others into the palace, enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu, and urged the Zhao forces to hasten west into the passes.

sentences.zh: 趙王將相相與謀曰：「王王趙，非楚意也。

translations.literal: Zhao king generals chancellors mutually plotted said: 'King king Zhao, not Chu intention.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao and his generals and ministers deliberated among themselves: 'The king became King of Zhao without Chu's approval.

sentences.zh: 楚已誅秦，必加兵於趙。

translations.literal: Once Chu has executed Qin, it will surely add troops against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chu has destroyed Qin, it will surely turn its armies against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 計莫如毋西兵，使使北徇燕地以自廣也。

translations.literal: The best plan is not to send troops west, but to send envoys north to sweep Yan lands and broaden ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The best plan is not to send troops westward but to dispatch forces north to take the Yan territories and expand our base.

sentences.zh: 趙南據大河，北有燕、代，楚雖勝秦，不敢制趙。

translations.literal: Zhao occupies the great river to the south and has Yan and Dai to the north. Even if Chu defeats Qin, it will not dare control Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: With the Yellow River to our south and Yan and Dai to the north, even if Chu defeats Qin, it would not dare try to subdue Zhao.

sentences.zh: 若楚不勝秦，必重趙。

translations.literal: If Chu does not defeat Qin, it will surely value Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: And if Chu fails to defeat Qin, it will be forced to rely on Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙乘秦之獘，可以得志於天下。」

translations.literal: Zhao take advantage Qin fatigue, can achieve ambitions in world.'
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao exploits Qin's weakness, we can achieve our ambitions in the empire.'

sentences.zh: 趙王以為然，因不西兵，而遣故上谷卒史韓廣將兵北徇燕地。

translations.literal: The Zhao king thought this right, so he did not send troops west. Instead, he sent the former Shanggu adjutant Han Guang to lead troops north and sweep through Yan lands.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao agreed. Rather than sending his forces west, he dispatched Han Guang, formerly a minor official in Shanggu, to lead an army north and subdue the Yan territories.

sentences.zh: 燕故貴人豪傑謂韓廣曰：「楚已立王，趙又已立王。

translations.literal: Yan former nobles outstanding men told Han Guang said: 'Chu already established king, Zhao also already established king.
translations.idiomatic: The old aristocrats and men of influence in Yan said to Han Guang, 'Chu has already set up a king, and Zhao has done likewise.

sentences.zh: 燕雖小，亦萬乘之國也，願將軍立為燕王。」

translations.literal: Yan though small, also ten thousand chariots country, wish general establish as Yan king.'
translations.idiomatic: Though Yan is small, it too was once a state of ten thousand chariots. We beg the general to declare himself King of Yan.'

sentences.zh: 韓廣曰：「廣母在趙，不可。」

translations.literal: Han Guang said: 'Guang mother in Zhao, cannot.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Guang replied, 'My mother is in Zhao. I cannot accept.'

sentences.zh: 燕人曰：「趙方西憂秦，南憂楚，其力不能禁我。

translations.literal: Yan people said: 'Zhao currently west worries Qin, south worries Chu, its strength cannot prohibit us.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Yan said, 'Zhao is beset by Qin to the west and Chu to the south — it has no strength to threaten us.

sentences.zh: 且以楚之彊，不敢害趙王將相之家，趙獨安敢害將軍之家！」

translations.literal: Moreover, with Chu strength, not dare harm Zhao king generals chancellors families, Zhao alone how dare harm general family!'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even mighty Chu has not dared to harm the families of the King of Zhao and his ministers. How then would Zhao alone dare harm the general's family?'

sentences.zh: 韓廣以為然，乃自立為燕王。

translations.literal: Han Guang thought this right and then established himself as Yan king.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guang found their reasoning persuasive and declared himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 居數月，趙奉燕王母及家屬歸之燕。

translations.literal: After several months, Zhao presented the Yan king's mother and family and returned them to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After several months, Zhao indeed returned the King of Yan's mother and his family to Yan.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，諸將之徇地者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: At this time, the various generals sweeping through lands were too numerous to count.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, the various generals campaigning across the land were too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 周市北徇地至狄，狄人田儋殺狄令，自立為齊王，以齊反擊周市。

translations.literal: Zhou Shi swept north through the lands and arrived at Di. The Di person Tian Dan killed the Di magistrate and established himself as Qi king. With Qi he counterattacked Zhou Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi marched north as far as Di, where Tian Dan, a man of Di, killed the local magistrate, declared himself King of Qi, and turned the forces of Qi against Zhou Shi.

sentences.zh: 市軍散，還至魏地，欲立魏後故甯陵君咎為魏王。

translations.literal: Shi's army scattered. He returned to Wei lands and wished to establish Jiu, the former Lord of Ningling and Wei descendant, as Wei king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi's forces were scattered. He withdrew to the Wei territories, intending to install Jiu, the Lord of Ningling and a descendant of the Wei royal house, as King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 時咎在陳王所，不得之魏。

translations.literal: At the time Jiu was at the Chen king's court and could not go to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, however, Jiu was at the court of the King of Chen and could not go to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏地已定，欲相與立周市為魏王，周市不肯。

translations.literal: The Wei lands were already pacified. They wished to mutually establish Zhou Shi as Wei king, but Zhou Shi was not willing.
translations.idiomatic: With the Wei territories already secured, the people wished to make Zhou Shi the King of Wei, but Zhou Shi refused.

sentences.zh: 使者五反，陳王乃立甯陵君咎為魏王，遣之國。

translations.literal: Envoys went back and forth five times. The Chen king then established Lord Jiu of Ningling as Wei king and sent him to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys traveled back and forth five times before the King of Chen finally installed the Lord of Ningling, Jiu, as King of Wei and sent him to his domain.

sentences.zh: 周市卒為相。

translations.literal: Zhou Shi finally became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi ultimately served as his chancellor.

sentences.zh: 將軍田臧等相與謀曰：「周章軍已破矣，秦兵旦暮至，我圍滎陽城弗能下，秦軍至，必大敗。

translations.literal: General Tian Zang etc. mutually plotted said: 'Zhou Zhang army already broken, Qin troops morning evening arrive, I besiege Xing Yang city not able conquer, Qin army arrives, must greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: General Tian Zang and the other officers conferred among themselves: 'Zhou Zhang's army has already been destroyed, and the Qin forces will be upon us any day now. We have laid siege to Xingyang but cannot take it. When the Qin army arrives, we will surely be routed.

sentences.zh: 不如少遺兵，足以守滎陽，悉精兵迎秦軍。

translations.literal: It would be better to leave a few troops, sufficient to guard Xingyang, and lead all the elite troops to meet the Qin army.
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave a small garrison sufficient to hold Xingyang and lead all our best troops out to meet the Qin army in the field.

sentences.zh: 今假王驕，不知兵權，不可與計，非誅之，事恐敗。」

translations.literal: Now acting king arrogant, not know military authority, cannot with plan, not execute him, matter fears fail.'
translations.idiomatic: The acting king has grown arrogant and knows nothing of military strategy. It is impossible to plan with him. Unless we remove him, our cause is doomed.'

sentences.zh: 因相與矯王令以誅吳叔，獻其首於陳王。

translations.literal: They therefore mutually forged the king's command to execute Wu Shu and presented his head to the Chen king.
translations.idiomatic: So they forged the king's orders to execute Wu Guang and presented his head to the King of Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳王使使賜田臧楚令尹印，使為上將。

translations.literal: The Chen king sent an envoy to give Tian Zang the Chu prime minister seal and made him supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen sent an envoy to bestow upon Tian Zang the seal of the Chu Prime Minister and appointed him Supreme General.

sentences.zh: 田臧乃使諸將李歸等守滎陽城，自以精兵西迎秦軍於敖倉。

translations.literal: Tian Zang then had the various generals Li Gui and others guard Xingyang city, while he himself led elite troops west to meet the Qin army at Aocang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zang ordered General Li Gui and others to hold the siege at Xingyang, while he himself led his best troops west to engage the Qin army at Aocang.

sentences.zh: 與戰，田臧死，軍破。

translations.literal: They fought, Tian Zang died, and the army was broken.
translations.idiomatic: They joined battle, and Tian Zang was killed. His army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 章邯進兵擊李歸等滎陽下，破之，李歸等死。

translations.literal: Zhang Han advanced his troops and attacked Li Gui and others below Xingyang. He broke them, and Li Gui and others died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han then advanced and attacked Li Gui and the others at Xingyang, smashing their forces. Li Gui and the rest were killed.

sentences.zh: 陽城人鄧說將兵居郯，章邯別將擊破之，鄧說軍散走陳。

translations.literal: Deng Yue of Yangcheng led troops and resided at Tan. Zhang Han's separate general attacked and broke them. Deng Yue's army scattered and fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue of Yangcheng had stationed troops at Tan. One of Zhang Han's subordinate generals attacked and routed them, and the remnants of Deng Yue's army scattered and fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 铚人伍徐將兵居許，章邯擊破之，伍徐軍皆散走陳。

translations.literal: Wu Xu of Zhi led troops and was stationed at Xu. Zhang Han attacked and defeated him, and Wu Xu's entire army scattered and fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xu of Zhi had stationed troops at Xu. Zhang Han attacked and defeated them as well, and Wu Xu's entire force scattered and fled back to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳王誅鄧說。

translations.literal: The Chen king executed Deng Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen had Deng Yue executed.

sentences.zh: 陳王初立時，陵人秦嘉、铚人董緶符離人朱雞石、取慮人鄭布、徐人丁疾等皆特起，將兵圍東海守慶於郯。

translations.literal: When the Chen king was first established, Qin Jia of Ling, Dong Xie of Zhi, Zhu Jishi of Fuli, Zheng Bu of Qulu, Ding Ji of Xu and others all rose up specially. They led troops and surrounded Governor Qing of Donghai at Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Chen was first enthroned, Qin Jia of Ling, Dong Xie of Zhi, Zhu Jishi of Fuli, Zheng Bu of Qulü, Ding Ji of Xu, and others had each risen independently. They led their troops to besiege Qing, the Governor of Donghai, at Tan.

sentences.zh: 陳王聞，乃使武平君畔為將軍，監郯下軍。

translations.literal: The Chen king heard and then made Lord Pan of Wuping a general to oversee the army below Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Chen heard of this, he appointed Pan, the Lord of Wuping, as general to supervise the forces besieging Tan.

sentences.zh: 秦嘉不受命，嘉自立為大司馬，惡屬武平君。

translations.literal: Qin Jia did not accept the command. Jia established himself as grand marshal and hated being subordinate to Lord Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jia refused to accept these orders. He declared himself Grand Marshal and resented being placed under the Lord of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 告軍吏曰：「武平君年少，不知兵事，勿聽！」

translations.literal: Told army officials said: 'Wu Ping lord young, not know military matters, do not listen!'
translations.idiomatic: He told the army officers, 'The Lord of Wuping is young and knows nothing of warfare. Do not take orders from him!'

sentences.zh: 因矯以王命殺武平君畔。

translations.literal: Therefore, he forged the king's command and killed Lord Pan of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: He then forged a royal order and had the Lord of Wuping killed.

sentences.zh: 章邯已破伍徐，擊陳，柱國房君死。

translations.literal: After defeating Wu Xu, Zhang Han attacked Chen, and the Lord of Fang, Pillar of State, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Wu Xu, Zhang Han attacked Chen itself. The Supreme Pillar of State, the Lord of Fang, was killed.

sentences.zh: 章邯又進兵擊陳西張賀軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Han again advanced his troops and attacked Zhang He's army west of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han then advanced further and struck the forces of Zhang He to the west of Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳王出監戰，軍破，張賀死。

translations.literal: The Chen king went out to oversee the battle. The army was broken, and Zhang He died.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen himself went out to oversee the battle, but his army was shattered and Zhang He was killed.

sentences.zh: 臘月，陳王之汝陰，還至下城父，其御莊賈殺以降秦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Chen king went to Ruyin. On his return to Xiachengfu, his charioteer Zhuang Jia killed him and surrendered to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the King of Chen traveled to Ruyin. On his return, at Xiachengfu, his own charioteer Zhuang Jia murdered him and surrendered to Qin.

sentences.zh: 陳勝葬碭，謚曰隱王。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng was buried at Dang with the posthumous name of Hidden King.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng was buried at Dang and given the posthumous title of 'the Hidden King.'

sentences.zh: 陳王故涓人將軍呂臣為倉頭軍，起新陽，攻陳下之，殺莊賈，復以陳為楚。

translations.literal: The Chen king's former attendant General Lu Chen organized a granary head army. He rose at Xinyang, attacked Chen and took it, killed Zhuang Jia, and again made Chen into Chu.
translations.idiomatic: General Lü Chen, a former palace attendant of the King of Chen, raised an army of 'Granary Heads.' He launched his campaign from Xinyang, attacked and retook the city of Chen, killed Zhuang Jia, and restored Chen to the banner of Chu.

sentences.zh: 初，陳王至陳，令铚人宋留將兵定南陽，入武關。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Chen king arrived at Chen, he ordered Song Liu of Zhi to lead troops to pacify Nanyang and enter Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the King of Chen first arrived at Chen, he had ordered Song Liu of Zhi to lead troops to pacify Nanyang and enter the Wu Pass.

sentences.zh: 留已徇南陽，聞陳王死，南陽復為秦。

translations.literal: Liu had already swept through Nanyang. When he heard the Chen king had died, Nanyang again became Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Song Liu had already subdued Nanyang, but upon hearing that the King of Chen was dead, Nanyang reverted to Qin.

sentences.zh: 宋留不能入武關，乃東至新蔡，遇秦軍，宋留以軍降秦。

translations.literal: Song Liu could not enter Wuguan. He then went east to Xincai, encountered Qin troops, and Song Liu surrendered his army to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to enter the Wu Pass, Song Liu retreated eastward to Xincai, where he encountered a Qin army and surrendered his forces.

sentences.zh: 秦傳留至咸陽，車裂留以徇。

translations.literal: Qin transported Liu to Xianyang and executed him by cart tearing as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had Song Liu transferred to Xianyang, where he was torn apart by chariots as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 秦嘉等聞陳王軍破出走，乃立景駒為楚王，引兵之方與，欲擊秦軍定陶下。

translations.literal: Qin Jia and others heard that the Chen king's army was broken and he had fled. They then established Jing Ju as Chu king, led troops to Fangyu, and wished to attack the Qin army below Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Jia and the others heard that the King of Chen's army had been destroyed and that he had fled, they set up Jing Ju as the new King of Chu, marched their forces to Fangyu, and prepared to attack the Qin army at Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 使公孫慶使齊王，欲與并力俱進。

translations.literal: They sent Gongsun Qing as envoy to the Qi king, wishing to combine forces and advance together.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Gongsun Qing as an envoy to the King of Qi, hoping to join forces and advance together.

sentences.zh: 齊王曰：「聞陳王戰敗，不知其死生，楚安得不請而立王！」

translations.literal: Qi king said: 'Heard Chen king battle defeated, not know his life death, Chu how not ask established king!'
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qi said, 'I have heard that the King of Chen has been defeated in battle, and no one knows whether he is alive or dead. How dare Chu set up a new king without consulting anyone?'

sentences.zh: 公孫慶曰：「齊不請楚而立王，楚何故請齊而立王！

translations.literal: Gongsun Qing said: 'Qi not ask Chu established king, Chu why ask Qi established king!
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Qing retorted, 'Qi did not consult Chu before setting up its own king — why should Chu consult Qi?

sentences.zh: 且楚首事，當令於天下。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Chu first matter, should command world.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it was Chu that first raised the standard of revolt — it is Chu that should command the empire.'

sentences.zh: 田儋誅殺公孫慶。

translations.literal: Tian Dan executed Gongsun Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Dan had Gongsun Qing put to death.

sentences.zh: 秦左右校復攻陳，下之。

translations.literal: Qin's left and right commanders again attacked Chen and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin Left and Right Colonels attacked Chen once more and captured it.

sentences.zh: 呂將軍走，收兵復聚。

translations.literal: General Lu fled but gathered troops and assembled again.
translations.idiomatic: General Lü fled but rallied his troops and reformed his forces.

sentences.zh: 鄱盜當陽君黥布之兵相收，復擊秦左右校，破之青波，復以陳為楚。

translations.literal: The Po robbers and Lord Dangyang Ying Bu's troops gathered together. They again attacked Qin's left and right commanders, broke them at Qingbo, and again made Chen into Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined forces with the bandit chief of Po and the troops of Qing Bu, Lord of Dangyang. Together they attacked the Qin Left and Right Colonels, defeated them at Qingbo, and once again restored Chen to the banner of Chu.

sentences.zh: 會項梁立懷王孫心為楚王。

translations.literal: At this time, Xiang Liang established the Huai king's grandson Xin as Chu king.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture, Xiang Liang installed Xin, a grandson of King Huai of Chu, as the new King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 陳勝王凡六月。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng was king for altogether six months.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng reigned as king for a total of six months.

sentences.zh: 已為王，王陳。

translations.literal: He had already become king and made Chen his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Having been made king, he ruled from the city of Chen.

sentences.zh: 其故人嘗與庸耕者聞之，之陳，扣宮門曰：「吾欲見涉。」

translations.literal: His old friend once with hired plow heard it, went Chen, knocked palace gate said: 'I wish see She.'
translations.idiomatic: An old companion from his days as a hired laborer heard the news and traveled to Chen. He knocked at the palace gate and said, 'I wish to see She.'

sentences.zh: 宮門令欲縛之。

translations.literal: The palace gate official wished to bind him.
translations.idiomatic: The officer at the gate was about to have him seized.

sentences.zh: 自辯數，乃置，不肯為通。

translations.literal: He pleaded his own case several times; they then released him but refused to announce him.
translations.idiomatic: After the man pleaded his case several times, the guards let him go but refused to announce him.

sentences.zh: 陳王出，遮道而呼涉。

translations.literal: When the Chen king came out, the man blocked the road and called, 'She!'
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Chen came out on the road, the man blocked his path and called out, 'She!'

sentences.zh: 陳王聞之，乃召見，載與俱歸。

translations.literal: The Chen king heard of it and then summoned him for an audience. He carried him and returned together.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen heard him and summoned him to an audience. He took the man into his carriage and returned to the palace together.

sentences.zh: 入宮，見殿屋帷帳，客曰：「夥頤！

translations.literal: Entered palace, saw hall rooms curtains tents, guest said: 'Plenty!
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the palace and seeing the great halls hung with curtains and drapes, the visitor exclaimed, 'What abundance!

sentences.zh: 涉之為王沈沈者！」

translations.literal: How vast and imposing are Chen She's halls as king!'
translations.idiomatic: How vast and imposing are the halls of King Chen She!'

sentences.zh: 楚人謂多為夥，故天下傳之，夥涉為王，由陳涉始。

translations.literal: Chu people call much 'plenty,' so the world transmitted it. 'Plenty She became king' began from Chen She.
translations.idiomatic: In the dialect of Chu, the word for 'much' is 'huo.' From this arose the saying known throughout the empire: 'How grand She has become as king!' — a phrase that originated with Chen She.

sentences.zh: 客出入愈益發舒，言陳王故情。

translations.literal: The guest, entering and exiting, became increasingly relaxed and open, speaking of the Chen king's old feelings.
translations.idiomatic: As the visitor came and went more freely, he grew increasingly at ease and began to speak openly of the king's humble past.

sentences.zh: 或說陳王曰：「客愚無知，顓妄言，輕威。」

translations.literal: Someone advised the Chen king, saying: 'The guest is foolish and ignorant; he speaks rashly on his own and belittles your majesty.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised the King of Chen, 'This guest is foolish and ignorant; he speaks rashly on his own and belittles Your Majesty.'

sentences.zh: 陳王斬之。

translations.literal: The Chen king beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen had the man beheaded.

sentences.zh: 諸陳王故人皆自引去，由是無親陳王者。

translations.literal: All the Chen king's old friends withdrew themselves. From this, there were no more intimates of the Chen king.
translations.idiomatic: After this, all the King of Chen's old friends withdrew. From that time on, no one dared draw close to him.

sentences.zh: 陳王以朱房為中正，胡武為司過，主司群臣。

translations.literal: The Chen king made Zhu Fang central upright and Hu Wu overseer of faults, mainly to oversee the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen appointed Zhu Fang as Arbiter of Rectitude and Hu Wu as Inspector of Faults, entrusting them with overseeing his ministers.

sentences.zh: 諸將徇地，至，令之不是者，系而罪之，以苛察為忠。

translations.literal: The various generals swept through lands. When they arrived, they bound and punished those who did not follow orders correctly, taking harsh scrutiny as loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When generals returned from their campaigns, any who fell short of expectations were arrested and punished. These officials mistook petty severity for loyal service.

sentences.zh: 其所不善者，弗下吏，輒自治之。

translations.literal: Those he disliked he did not send to officials but promptly handled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Those they took a dislike to were not referred to the proper authorities but dealt with on their own.

sentences.zh: 陳王信用之。

translations.literal: The Chen king trusted and used them.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Chen placed his full trust in these men.

sentences.zh: 諸將以其故不親附，此其所以敗也。

translations.literal: The various generals because of this reason were not intimately attached. This was the reason he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the generals refused to give him their loyalty. This was the root cause of his downfall.

sentences.zh: 陳勝雖已死，其所置遣侯王將相竟亡秦，由涉首事也。

translations.literal: Though Chen Sheng was already dead, the marquises, kings, generals, and chancellors he established and dispatched ultimately destroyed Qin. It was She who first raised the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chen Sheng himself was already dead, the lords, kings, generals, and ministers he had appointed and dispatched ultimately destroyed Qin. It was She who lit the first flame.

sentences.zh: 高祖時為陳涉置守冢三十家碭，至今血食。

translations.literal: During the time of Emperor Gaozu, thirty households were established at Dang to guard Chen She's tomb. Sacrifices are offered there to this day.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Gaozu, thirty households were established at Dang to tend Chen She's tomb. To this day, sacrifices are offered there.

sentences.zh: 褚先生曰：地形險阻，所以為固也；

translations.literal: Chu mister said: 'Terrain dangerous obstructed, reason for solid;
translations.idiomatic: Master Chu remarked: Rugged terrain is what provides a state with its defenses;

sentences.zh: 兵革刑法，所以為治也。

translations.literal: Arms, armor, punishments, and laws are what make governance.'
translations.idiomatic: arms, armor, punishments, and laws are what provide it with governance.

sentences.zh: 猶未足恃也。

translations.literal: Yet these are still not sufficient to rely on.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet none of these alone is sufficient to rely upon.

sentences.zh: 夫先王以仁義為本，而以固塞文法為枝葉，豈不然哉！

translations.literal: Indeed former kings with benevolence righteousness as root, and with solid barriers written laws as branches leaves, how not so!
translations.idiomatic: The former kings took benevolence and righteousness as the root, and fortifications and written law as the branches and leaves. Is this not so?

sentences.zh: 吾聞賈生之稱曰：

translations.literal: I heard Jia Sheng's words said:
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the words of Jia Yi, who said:

sentences.zh: 秦孝公據殽函之固，擁雍州之地，君臣固守，以窺周室。

translations.literal: Qin Xiao Gong occupied Xiao Han's solid, embraced Yong Zhou's lands, ruler ministers firmly guarded, to spy Zhou chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiao of Qin held the strongholds of Xiao and Hangu, commanded the lands of Yongzhou, and with ruler and ministers holding fast, cast his gaze upon the royal house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 有席卷天下，包舉宇內，囊括四海之意，并吞八荒之心。

translations.literal: He had the intention to roll up the world, package up the universe, embrace the four seas, and swallow the eight wastes.'
translations.idiomatic: He harbored the ambition to roll up the empire like a mat, to sweep all within the four seas into his arms, to engulf the eight horizons.

sentences.zh: 當是時也，商君佐之，內立法度，務耕織，修守戰之備；

translations.literal: At this time, Shang lord assisted him, internally established laws measures, devoted farming weaving, repaired defense battle preparations;
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Lord Shang assisted him: within, he established laws and standards, promoted agriculture and weaving, and built up the means of defense and war;

sentences.zh: 外連衡而鬬諸侯。

translations.literal: Externally he connected horizontally and fought the feudal lords.'
translations.idiomatic: without, he forged horizontal alliances to set the feudal lords against one another.

sentences.zh: 於是秦人拱手而取西河之外。

translations.literal: Thus, Qin people effortlessly took the lands west of the Xi River.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus, the people of Qin took the lands beyond the West River with folded arms.

sentences.zh: 孝公既沒，惠文王、武王、昭王蒙故業，因遺策，南取漢中，西舉巴蜀，東割膏腴之地，收要害之郡。

translations.literal: After Duke Xiao died, Kings Huiwen, Wu, and Zhao inherited his enterprise and followed his remaining plans. They took Hanzhong to the south, raised Bashu to the west, cut fertile lands to the east, and gathered strategic commanderies.'
translations.idiomatic: After Duke Xiao's death, Kings Huiwen, Wu, and Zhao carried on his legacy and followed his grand strategy. They seized Hanzhong to the south, conquered Ba and Shu to the west, carved away the fertile lands to the east, and secured the strategically vital commanderies.

sentences.zh: 諸侯恐懼，會盟而謀弱秦。

translations.literal: The feudal lords feared and assembled in alliance to plot weakening Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords were filled with dread. They convened alliances and plotted to weaken Qin.

sentences.zh: 不愛珍器重寶肥饒之地，以致天下之士。

translations.literal: They did not love precious vessels, heavy treasures, or fertile abundant lands, but used them to attract the world's scholars.'
translations.idiomatic: They spared no expense — neither precious vessels, rare treasures, nor fertile lands — all to attract the finest men the empire could offer.

sentences.zh: 合從締交，相與為一。

translations.literal: They combined vertically, concluded friendships, and mutually became one.'
translations.idiomatic: They forged the Vertical Alliance and bound themselves together as one.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，齊有孟嘗，趙有平原，楚有春申，魏有信陵：此四君者，皆明知而忠信，寬厚而愛人，尊賢而重士。

translations.literal: At this time, Qi had Meng Chang, Zhao had Ping Yuan, Chu had Chun Shen, Wei had Xin Ling: these four lords, all clear knowing loyal trustworthy, broad thick loved people, honored worthy valued scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Qi had Lord Mengchang, Zhao had Lord Pingyuan, Chu had Lord Chunshen, and Wei had Lord Xinling. These four lords were all men of keen discernment and steadfast loyalty, generous of spirit and devoted to their followers, who honored the worthy and valued men of talent.

sentences.zh: 約從連衡，兼韓、魏、燕、趙、宋、衛、中山之眾。

translations.literal: They covenanted vertically and connected horizontally, combining the multitudes of Han, Wei, Yan, Zhao, Song, Wei, and Zhongshan.'
translations.idiomatic: They pledged vertical and horizontal alliances and united the forces of Han, Wei, Yan, Zhao, Song, Wey, and Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 於是六國之士有甯越、徐尚、蘇秦、杜赫之屬為之謀，齊明、周聚、陳軫、邵滑、樓緩、翟景、蘇厲、樂毅之徒通其意，吳起、孫臏、帶他、兒良、王廖、田忌、廉頗、趙奢之倫制其兵。

translations.literal: Thus, the six states' scholars had Ning Yue, Xu Shang, Su Qin, and Du He and their kind to plan for them. Qi Ming, Zhou Ju, Chen Zhen, Shao Hua, Lou Huan, Di Jing, Su Li, and Yue Yi and their followers communicated their intentions. Wu Qi, Sun Bin, Dai Ta, Er Liang, Wang Liao, Tian Ji, Lian Po, and Zhao She and their sort controlled their troops.'
translations.idiomatic: The six states thus had men like Ning Yue, Xu Shang, Su Qin, and Du He to devise their strategies; Qi Ming, Zhou Ju, Chen Zhen, Shao Hua, Lou Huan, Di Jing, Su Li, and Yue Yi to serve as their intermediaries; and Wu Qi, Sun Bin, Dai Tuo, Ni Liang, Wang Liao, Tian Ji, Lian Po, and Zhao She to command their armies.

sentences.zh: 嘗以什倍之地，百萬之師，仰關而攻秦。

translations.literal: Once with ten times the lands and a million troops, they looked up at the pass and attacked Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: Once, commanding territory tenfold greater than Qin's and armies a million strong, they marched upon the passes and attacked.

sentences.zh: 秦人開關而延敵，九國之師遁逃而不敢進。

translations.literal: The Qin people opened the pass and invited the enemy. The nine states' troops fled and dared not advance.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Qin opened their gates and advanced to meet them, the armies of the nine states turned and fled, not daring to engage.

sentences.zh: 秦無亡矢遺鏃之費，而天下固已困矣。

translations.literal: Qin expended not even a lost arrow or remaining arrowhead, yet the world was already distressed.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin did not lose a single arrow or arrowhead, yet the empire had already been brought to its knees.

sentences.zh: 於是從散約敗，爭割地而賂秦。

translations.literal: Thus, the vertical alliance scattered and the covenant was defeated. They contended to cut lands and bribe Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: The Vertical Alliance disintegrated and its pacts collapsed. The states vied with one another to cede territory and bribe Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦有餘力而制其獘，追亡逐北，伏尸百萬，流血漂櫓，因利乘便，宰割天下，分裂山河，彊國請服，弱國入朝。

translations.literal: Qin had surplus strength and controlled their fatigue. They pursued the fleeing and chased to the north. A million corpses lay prostrate, blood flowed to float oars. Taking advantage and multiplying convenience, they butchered the world, split mountains and rivers. Strong states requested submission, weak states entered court.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin, with strength to spare, exploited their rivals' exhaustion. It pursued the routed and chased down the fleeing. Corpses lay in heaps of a million; blood ran until it could float shields. Seizing every advantage, Qin carved up the empire, partitioned mountains and rivers. The strong states begged for submission; the weak presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 施及孝文王、莊襄王，享國之日淺，國家無事。

translations.literal: This extended to Kings Xiaowen and Zhuangxiang. The days they enjoyed ruling were few, and the state had no matters.'
translations.idiomatic: The reigns of Kings Xiaowen and Zhuangxiang were brief, and the state knew no great upheaval.

sentences.zh: 及至始皇，奮六世之餘烈，振長策而御宇內，吞二周而亡諸侯，履至尊而制六合，執敲樸以鞭笞天下，威振四海。

translations.literal: When it reached the First Emperor, he exerted the remaining brilliance of six generations, shook the long whip and drove the universe, swallowed the two Zhous and perished the feudal lords, trod the utmost honor and controlled the six directions, grasped the knocker club to whip and lash the world, his might shaking the four seas.'
translations.idiomatic: Then came the First Emperor. He took up the accumulated might of six generations, cracked his long whip and drove the whole world before him. He swallowed the Two Zhous and extinguished the feudal lords, ascended to the supreme position and imposed his will upon all within the six directions, wielding his rod to flog the empire into submission. His power shook the four seas.

sentences.zh: 南取百越之地，以為桂林、象郡，百越之君俛首系頸，委命下吏。

translations.literal: He took the Baiyue lands to the south and made them Guilin and Xiang commandery. The Baiyue lords bowed their heads and tied their necks, entrusting their lives to lower officials.'
translations.idiomatic: To the south, he seized the lands of the Hundred Yue and made them the commanderies of Guilin and Xiang. The chiefs of the Hundred Yue bowed their heads, placed ropes about their own necks, and entrusted their fates to Qin's petty officials.

sentences.zh: 乃使蒙恬北筑長城而守藩籬，卻匈奴七百餘里，胡人不敢南下而牧馬，士亦不敢貫弓而報怨。

translations.literal: He then had Meng Tian build the long wall to the north as a guarding fence, repelling the Xiongnu over seven hundred li. The Hu people dared not come south to pasture their horses, and scholars dared not draw their bows to report grievances.'
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Meng Tian to build the Great Wall to the north as a bulwark, driving the Xiongnu back more than seven hundred li. The Hu peoples no longer dared ride south to graze their horses, and warriors no longer dared string their bows to seek vengeance.

sentences.zh: 於是廢先王之道，燔百家之言，以愚黔首。

translations.literal: Thus, he abolished the former kings' way and burned the hundred schools' words to fool the black-headed people.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he cast aside the Way of the former kings and burned the writings of the Hundred Schools, all to keep the common people in ignorance.

sentences.zh: 墮名城，殺豪俊，收天下之兵聚之咸陽，銷鋒鍉，鑄以為金人十二，以弱天下之民。

translations.literal: He destroyed famous cities, killed outstanding men, gathered the world's weapons and assembled them at Xianyang, melted the sharp points, and cast them as twelve gold men to weaken the world's people.'
translations.idiomatic: He razed the great walls of famous cities, slaughtered the heroes and men of talent, confiscated all the weapons in the empire and gathered them at Xianyang, where he melted down the blades and arrowheads and cast them into twelve colossal bronze figures — all to weaken the people of the empire.

sentences.zh: 然後踐華為城，因河為池，據億丈之城，臨不測之谿以為固。

translations.literal: Then he trod on splendor as his city, took the river as his moat, occupied the hundred million zhang city, and faced the unfathomable gorge for security.'
translations.idiomatic: Then he set Mount Hua as his rampart and the Yellow River as his moat, perched atop walls ten thousand feet high, and looked down upon fathomless gorges as his defense.

sentences.zh: 良將勁弩，守要害之處，信臣精卒，陳利兵而誰何。

translations.literal: Good generals and strong crossbows guarded strategic places. Trustworthy ministers and elite troops displayed sharp weapons and challenged intruders.'
translations.idiomatic: Able generals with powerful crossbows guarded every strategic pass. Trusted ministers and elite soldiers arrayed their keen weapons and challenged all who approached.

sentences.zh: 天下已定，始皇之心，自以為關中之固，金城千里，子孫帝王萬世之業也。

translations.literal: The world was already pacified. In the First Emperor's heart, he thought Guanzhong's defenses solid, a gold city of a thousand li, an enterprise for descendants to be emperor and king for ten thousand generations.'
translations.idiomatic: With the empire settled, the First Emperor believed in his heart that the stronghold within the passes, that impregnable fortress stretching a thousand li, would be the foundation of an imperial dynasty lasting ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 始皇既沒，餘威振於殊俗。

translations.literal: The First Emperor had already died, yet his remaining might shook different customs.'
translations.idiomatic: After the First Emperor died, his lingering authority still overawed distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 然而陳涉甕牖繩樞之子，甿隸之人，而遷徙之徒也。

translations.literal: However, Chen She was the son of an urn-window rope-pivot family, a rural servant person, and a migrant.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chen She was the son of a family so poor their windows were broken jars and their door-hinges were made of rope — a field laborer and a conscript exile.

sentences.zh: 材能不及中人，非有仲尼、墨翟之賢，陶朱、猗頓之富也。

translations.literal: His talent and ability did not reach the average person. He did not have Confucius or Mozi's wisdom, or Tao Zhu or Yidun's wealth.'
translations.idiomatic: His talents did not surpass those of an ordinary man. He possessed neither the wisdom of Confucius or Mozi, nor the wealth of Tao Zhu or Yi Dun.

sentences.zh: 躡足行伍之閒，俛仰仟佰之中，率罷散之卒，將數百之眾，轉而攻秦。

translations.literal: He stepped among the ranks and files, bent and raised among the thousand and hundred, led exhausted scattered troops, commanded a multitude of several hundred, and turned to attack Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks of common soldiers, looked about him amid the files and columns, led a ragged band of weary conscripts — a force of a mere few hundred — and turned to attack Qin.

sentences.zh: 斬木為兵，揭竿為旗，天下雲會響應，贏糧而景從，山東豪俊遂并起而亡秦族矣。

translations.literal: He cut wood for weapons, raised poles for banners. The world gathered like clouds and echoed in response. They carried grain and followed like shadows. The Shandong outstanding men then rose together and destroyed the Qin clan.'
translations.idiomatic: They cut down trees for weapons and raised bamboo poles for banners. The people of the empire gathered like clouds, answered like echoes, carried their provisions on their backs, and followed like shadows. The heroes east of the mountains rose as one and brought the house of Qin to ruin.

sentences.zh: 且天下非小弱也；

translations.literal: Moreover, world not small weak;
translations.idiomatic: Now, the empire had not grown smaller or weaker;

sentences.zh: 雍州之地，殽函之固自若也。

translations.literal: Yongzhou's lands and Xiao and Hangu's defenses were as before.
translations.idiomatic: the lands of Yongzhou and the fortress of Xiao and Hangu were as formidable as ever.

sentences.zh: 陳涉之位，非尊於齊、楚、燕、趙、韓、魏、宋、衛、中山之君也；

translations.literal: Chen She's position was not more exalted than the lords of Qi, Chu, Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei, Song, Wey, and Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: Chen She's station was not more exalted than the lords of Qi, Chu, Yan, Zhao, Han, Wei, Song, Wey, and Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 鉏耰棘矜，非铦於句戟長鎩也；

translations.literal: Plow rake thorn shaft, not sharp than hooked halberd long spear;
translations.idiomatic: hoes and rakes and sharpened stakes were no match for hooked halberds and long spears;

sentences.zh: 適戍之眾，非儔於九國之師也；

translations.literal: Going garrison multitude, not equal nine states troops;
translations.idiomatic: a band of garrison conscripts could not compare with the armies of nine states;

sentences.zh: 深謀遠慮，行軍用兵之道，非及鄉時之士也。

translations.literal: His deep plans and far considerations, the way of marching and using troops, did not reach the scholars of former times.
translations.idiomatic: and in grand strategy and the arts of war, Chen She could not approach the statesmen and generals of earlier times.

sentences.zh: 然而成敗異變，功業相反也。

translations.literal: However, success and failure have different changes. Merit and enterprise are opposite.
translations.idiomatic: And yet the outcome was the very opposite of what one might expect: their successes and failures were completely reversed.

sentences.zh: 嘗試使山東之國與陳涉度長絜大，比權量力，則不可同年而語矣。

translations.literal: Try to make the Shandong states measure length and compare greatness with Chen She, compare authority and measure strength, and they cannot be spoken of in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: If one were to compare the states east of the mountains with Chen She — measuring their territory, weighing their power and resources — they could not even be mentioned in the same breath.

sentences.zh: 然而秦以區區之地。

translations.literal: However, Qin with its small lands,
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qin, starting from its modest territory,

sentences.zh: 致萬乘之權，抑八州而朝同列，百有餘年矣。

translations.literal: achieved the authority of ten thousand chariots, suppressed the eight provinces and made the same rank come to court, for over a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: rose to command a force of ten thousand chariots, subjugated the eight provinces, and forced its peers to pay court — for more than a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 然後以六合為家，殽函為宮。

translations.literal: Then took the six directions as home and Xiao and Hangu as palace.
translations.idiomatic: Then at last it made all within the six directions its home and the passes of Xiao and Hangu its palace.

sentences.zh: 一夫作難而七廟墮，身死人手，為天下笑者，何也？

translations.literal: One man made difficulty seven temples fell, body died people hands, became world laughter, what?
translations.idiomatic: Yet a single commoner raised a revolt and the seven ancestral temples came crashing down. The ruler died at the hands of others and became the laughingstock of the empire. Why?

sentences.zh: 仁義不施，而攻守之勢異也。

translations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness were not applied, but the situation of attack and defense was different.'
translations.idiomatic: Because benevolence and righteousness were not practiced, and the balance between offensive and defensive power had shifted.
